cross_review.rationale: Confirmed in src/core/uci_sim_packet.c:52-62. For non-DATA packets the serializer clamps wire_len to 255 and still returns 0 (success). The caller has no way to detect the truncation. Combined with B2 this is the dominant transport regression.

send_to_client (uci_sim_tcp_server.c:43-57) serializes once and writes the resulting bytes — there is no PBF fragmentation. The previous transport handled UCI control fragmentation; this rewrite removes it. Anything that returns >255B of control payload (GET_APP_CONFIG_ALL, large GET_CALIBRATIONS, vendor-heavy DEVICE_INFO) is now broken on the wire.

Loop terminates correctly. jndex is uint8_t and key_len is also uint8_t (max 255). At jndex=254 the body runs, then jndex++ → 255 (no wrap, since 254+1 fits in uint8_t), the test 255 < key_len (where key_len ≤ 255) is false, and the loop exits. A hang would require key_len > 255, which the type forbids. The loop is benign.

Confirmed in uci_sim_tcp_server.c:98-111. For DATA packets the 16-bit declared length can exceed sizeof(pkt->payload)=UCI_SIM_MAX_PAYLOAD=1024; max is clamped, only max bytes are recv'd, then payload_len is overwritten with poff. The remaining declared-but-unread bytes stay in the kernel socket buffer and will be misinterpreted as the next header. Stream desync is real for DATA messages.

uci_sim_tcp_server.c:170-217: poll() returns either at the 50 ms timeout OR immediately on client data, but uci_sim_engine_tick(engine, ENGINE_TICK_MS) is unconditionally called once per iteration. Burst command traffic causes virtual time to advance many multiples of 50 ms in milliseconds of wall time. Scheduled notifications (range events) fire ahead of intended cadence. Real semantic regression vs. the prior clock-driven loop.

Confirmed in uci_sim_profile.c:560-566 — the function returns 1 unconditionally and a comment explicitly documents the choice. While the intent (permissive storage) is plausibly deliberate, two problems remain: (1) NULL profile yields 1, inconsistent with sibling supports_* functions that NULL-check, and (2) custom profiles with intentionally narrow supported_session_app_config lists are silently bypassed.

Confirmed. send() at uci_sim_tcp_server.c:52 uses flags=0; sigaction (lines 126-131) only installs SIGTERM; no SIGPIPE handler or SIG_IGN, and no SO_NOSIGPIPE. Any peer disconnect during a flush of a notification can kill the simulator process via SIGPIPE, defeating SIGTERM-based test teardown semantics.

Confirmed at uci_sim_handlers.c:289-291. When offset + key_len > request->payload_len the loop breaks but the response still carries UCI_STATUS_OK with num_returned reflecting only the keys that fit. Malformed input should produce UCI_STATUS_INVALID_MSG_SIZE, not a silently partial OK.

Confirmed at uci_sim_handlers.c:383-407. payload_len is clamped to 255 but payload[9] is always written as vendor_len & 0xFF. For vendor_len > 245 the response asserts more vendor bytes than the packet actually contains, and once fragmentation is restored (per B2) the cap-to-255 here should be removed entirely.

additions.title: SIGTERM is swallowed while blocked in recv — clean shutdown is unreliable
additions.description: uci_sim_tcp_server.c installs SIGTERM with sa_flags=0 (no SA_RESTART) but read_command (lines 81-87, 102-109) explicitly continues on EINTR. When the server is blocked in recv waiting for client data, SIGTERM interrupts the syscall, the handler sets g_shutdown=1, but read_command immediately retries recv instead of returning to the loop. The g_shutdown flag is only consulted between loop iterations, so the process cannot terminate until the client happens to send (or close) something. This breaks the documented 'SIGTERM for test teardown' contract. Fix: in EINTR branches, check g_shutdown and bail out, or do not handle EINTR at all and let the loop re-poll.

additions.title: Second-client connections are accepted then silently dropped
additions.description: uci_sim_tcp_server.c:189-194 accepts incoming connections on listen_fd while a primary client is connected, then immediately close()s them without sending anything. From the secondary client's POV the TCP connection succeeds but the very next read returns EOF. This produces confusing, racy test failures rather than a deterministic 'busy' or refuse-to-accept response. Either stop accepting (poll only client_fd once paired) or send a deterministic error and shutdown(SHUT_WR) before close.

additions.title: Flush after engine_tick can attempt send on a half-closed peer
additions.description: uci_sim_tcp_server.c:210-216 checks POLLERR/POLLHUP/POLLNVAL only after the POLLIN branch and AFTER the unconditional engine_tick/flush_to_client call. If poll signals POLLIN|POLLHUP because the client did a half-close, read_command may succeed reading the queued bytes, then flush_to_client tries to write a response/notification to a peer that has FIN'd. Combined with the missing SIGPIPE handling (B7), this is a realistic crash trigger for graceful disconnects. The hangup check should run before any write attempt.

summary: I validate 8 of 9 of B's findings. Transport regressions (B1/B2 truncation, B4 desync, B5 time skew, B7 SIGPIPE) are the load-bearing blockers. I challenge B3: the uint8_t loop terminates correctly; no hang is reachable. I add a major shutdown bug (SIGTERM swallowed in recv) and two minor connection-lifecycle concerns.
